cohort: 19,864 women admitted in relation to pregnancy, childbirth, or postpartum complications (2.9% were asylum seekers)
finding: Asylum-seeking women were at higher risk of abortive outcomes/stillbirths and showed a tendency towards higher postnatal complications compared to residents, highlighting a need for improved outpatient postnatal care for this population.
mod_finding: This study found that asylum seeking women had lower odds of cesarean sections compared to residents.
